pages.text: Rain poured outside the window. Dad, in his overalls, took Pongi's boots from their place. "Pongi, shall you try putting them on by yourself today?" Pongi clenched both paws by her chest. "By myself! I'll do it myself!"
Pongi pushed a foot into a boot. Oh! It stopped halfway. Even when she held the boot in both paws and pushed, her heel got stuck. She toppled backward. "Oh, it won't work!"
One boot lay far away. "Pongi can't even put on boots..." She hung her head. She wanted to splash in the puddles outside, but she felt upset.
Dad sat beside Pongi and held up the boot. "This isn't a boot. It's a deep tunnel. Your toes just need to go right to the end." Dad opened the top of the boot into a circle with his paws.
Knock, knock! Grandpa Goose, the canal keeper in boots, stood at the door. "I'm going to check the bank. Coming with me, Pongi?" Pongi picked up the fallen boot again.
First, toes into the tunnel! Sitting down, Pongi gently pushed her toes in. They reached the end. Dad sang, "Toes first, into your boots!"
Second, heel in! Pongi held the top of the boot in both paws and pulled. Her heel slipped in. One foot had a boot, and one was bare. Grandpa said from the doorway, "That's it! Just like me!"
The other foot too: toes first, heel in! Pongi stood and stamped. Both feet had boots! She thumped her tail. "Toes first, into your boots! I did it myself!" she called.

On a rainy day, Pongi put on her boots alone in the doorway. "One, toes into the tunnel! Two, hold the top and pull your heel in! Three, stand up and stamp!" Boots on both feet! Today she had done it all herself.

Dad lifted Pongi's two booted feet into the air. "These feet can do it all by themselves now!" Boots are tunnels for your toes to go into first. "Toes first, into your boots! Dad, let's splash in the puddles!"
